checks.finding: T-010 (Risk: medium) implements the same security-relevant track-selection precedence logic that T-011 (Risk: high) implements for the remaining two consumers. T-010's Goal states it revises bootstrap/SKILL.md, sdd-bootstrap-interviewer/SKILL.md, and lite-gate/SKILL.md per design.md's four-case rule: absent -> compatibility fallback; present+valid -> new precedence; present-but-failing-REQ-005-validation -> explicit PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID stop, never treated as absent. This is the exact ADR-0023 access-control precedence fix (security-spec.md's B5 'Track-selection fail-open' boundary; AC-025/AC-026/AC-039 test all 5 REQ-009 consumers identically per traceability.md's REQ-009 row and AC-039's 30-assertion, 5-consumer x 6-case matrix). T-010's own Risk Rationale claims these 3 consumers 'implement no new security-decision logic themselves,' but its Goal/Scope text describes exactly the PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID-vs-fallback decision branch being added to these files. Per risk-classification-policy.md's high tier ('access control ... anything where a silent defect causes material harm') and by direct parity with T-011's high classification for the identical behavior class in the other 2 of the same 5 consumers, T-010 is under-classified; a silent defect in this precedence logic (e.g. a present-but-invalid Context mistakenly treated as absent) reproduces exactly the 'silent downgrade' ADR-0023 exists to close.

Every Risk: high/critical task (T-002,T-003,T-004,T-005,T-006,T-007,T-008,T-009,T-011) includes in its Done When section both TDD Red/Green evidence recorded in the implementation report and an independent quality-gate verdict (a named second reviewer) recording PASS (e.g. T-002's, T-005's, T-009's final Done-When bullets). Both Risk: critical tasks (T-006, T-008) additionally include 'a second, distinct named approver additionally reviews and signs the evidence bundle (Risk: critical, risk-classification-policy.md:17)' in their final Done-When bullet, satisfying the additional critical-tier requirement. No high/critical task omits any of the required Done-When evidence items.

T-004 ('Author the approver registry schema and the policy-weakening detector') bundles two structurally distinct implementation artifacts under one task -- a new JSON Schema (contracts/approver-registry.schema.json) and a separate algorithmic script (detect-policy-weakening.py, implementing the 3-implemented/6-N/A weakening-category table, the glob-coverage narrowing algorithm, and the approved-context anchor CLI resolution) -- and its Done When list has 11 distinct verifiable items (TEST-044, TEST-045, TEST-046, TEST-016, TEST-017, TEST-018, TEST-030, TEST-031, suite self-registration, CHANGELOG update, TDD Red/Green+independent-review evidence), exceeding the 8-item oversized-task threshold. The task title itself joins the two artifacts with 'and'. T-001 ('Author the project-context.yaml and provider-bindings.yaml schemas') shows the same pattern less severely (3 bundled schema/template artifacts, 11 Done-When items), and T-003 (schema + staging-only signer) is a milder instance at 9 Done-When items. Splitting T-004 into a schema-authoring task and a detector-algorithm task, mirroring how T-002/T-005 each own a single artifact, would make each unit completable in a single focused session with per-artifact TDD/review evidence rather than conflated evidence across two functionally unrelated deliverables.

Every functional task's underlying REQ has dedicated, explicit error-path/edge-case acceptance criteria distinct from happy-path coverage: T-001/REQ-001-002 (AC-001/AC-003 parameterized negative fixture sets, AC-040 duplicate-id rejection), T-002/REQ-003 (AC-005 four-category rejection lock, AC-037 boundary-vector rejections), T-003/REQ-004 (AC-010 negative schema fixtures, AC-011 fail-closed-with-no-key), T-004/REQ-006 (AC-044 malformed-registry rejection, AC-045 duplicate-id rejection), T-005/REQ-005 (AC-014 six-way negative proof), T-006/REQ-007 (AC-033 symlink/hard-link/crash-injection edge cases), T-007/REQ-010 (AC-027 write-executed/unrecognized/missing/stale-nonce rejection cases, AC-032 cleanup-failure/stale-sentinel cases), T-010/T-011/REQ-009 (AC-026 PROJECT_CONTEXT_INVALID explicit-stop case distinct from the absent-fallback happy path). No functional task's REQ is covered by happy-path-only acceptance criteria.

acceptance-tests.md's own header states TEST IDs (TEST-001..TEST-046) map 1:1 to AC-001..AC-046 -- every test task in tasks.md cites TEST-NNN IDs that are, by this package's own consistent design, acceptance tests each tied to one specific AC-NNN (satisfying the check's acceptance-test criterion 'must reference a specific AC-NNN'), e.g. T-001's Done When ties TEST-001 to (AC-001), TEST-002 to (AC-002), etc., across every task. Every Risk: high/critical task carries a task-specific Rollback: field: T-002 ('revert this task's two commits; nothing protected is touched yet'), T-003 ('a staged candidate that is never applied leaves no live-state change to roll back'), T-006 ('no protected file is touched by this task ... T-008 does that later'), T-008 ('reverting this task's agent-authored commit does NOT automatically revert an already-human-applied guard-invariants.json/generated-file change -- the revert PR states explicitly whether a human should also hand-revert that application'), T-011 (identical human-applied-change caveat for ship/SKILL.md and lite-spec/SKILL.md). Each addresses the specific revert mechanics for its own artifact class (staged-only vs. human-applied vs. protected).

tests/run-all.sh/.ps1 and the staged specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/human-copy/.github/workflows/test.yml + MANIFEST.sha256 are claimed as Planned Files by all 12 tasks, and Global Constraints requires each task to append 'in this task list's own numeric order (T-001 through T-012), one array-append per task ... so no two tasks race on the same shared file' -- but this ordering is not enforced via the Blockers field for every task. T-002 (2nd in numeric order) declares Blockers: None despite sharing these files with T-001 (1st); T-004 (4th) declares Blockers: T-002 only, omitting T-003 (3rd, the immediately preceding numeric-order task); T-006 (6th) and T-007 (7th) each declare Blockers: None despite sharing these files with T-001 through T-005/T-006 respectively. SCOPE-DISJOINT's own legitimate-sharing carve-out requires 'the Blockers field enforces the ordering' -- for these tasks it does not, so a downstream orchestrator relying on the Blockers graph could legitimately schedule e.g. T-003 and T-004 in parallel or out of order, racing on the same shared append-only files Global Constraints exists to protect.

The numeric-order append chain for the shared files (tests/run-all.sh/.ps1, the staged .github/workflows/test.yml candidate, MANIFEST.sha256) is broken/non-transitive at several points: T-008 (8th in numeric order) declares Blockers: T-002,T-003,T-004,T-005,T-006,T-007 but omits T-001 (1st); T-010 (10th) declares Blockers: T-001,T-005,T-007 but omits T-008 and T-009 (8th/9th, the immediately preceding numeric-order tasks for the shared append); T-011 (11th) declares Blockers: T-008,T-010 but omits T-009 (9th). Combined with T-002/T-004/T-006/T-007 also not blocking on their own immediately-preceding numeric-order task (see SCOPE-DISJOINT finding), the overall Blockers graph does not guarantee the strict per-task landing order Global Constraints mandates for these shared files ('so no two tasks race on the same shared file') -- an omission that would cause exactly the integration failure (a lost or conflicting array-append, or a corrupted staged MANIFEST.sha256) this check's missing-blockers condition addresses. Only T-001, T-003, T-005, T-009, and T-012 currently have Blockers consistent with the required numeric-order chain.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. T-001 through T-012 are all net-new schema/tool authoring, protected-file registration, or verification/audit tasks (e.g. T-009's Goal is to 'Prove, against the LIVE, post-T-008-application hook guard, that a write attempt ... is denied' -- a security-verification task confirming NEW protection just registered, not a regression fix for pre-existing broken behavior); none of T-001..T-012's title, Goal, Scope, or Done When describes fixing an existing defect, regression, or flaky test.
